reason: The text extensively emphasizes strict hierarchical structures throughout. It depicts clear chains of command with kings (Hezekiah and Sennacherib) at the apex, specific titled officials (Tartan, Rab-saris, Rab-shakeh, Eliakim, Shebna, Joah) executing their roles, submission of one nation to another through tribute, and obedience to royal commands. The narrative structure itself is built on hierarchical relationships—between conqueror and conquered, kings and their servants, and ultimately God's supremacy over all earthly powers. Rather than being unimportant or discouraged, strict hierarchy is fundamental to the text's political and theological framework.
